title: FAMtastic campaign posting schedule
description: The one file that makes a campaign postable. scripts/queue-campaign-drops.py reads this and needs no per-campaign code. Every campaign differs in cadence, channels, media, and copy, so all of that lives here as data rather than in a bespoke script. Scaffold with scripts/new-campaign.py.

campaign_id.description: Stable snake_case campaign identifier used in UTM attribution.

program_id.description: The offer/SKU this campaign sells, e.g. FAM-FOOT-199. Groups every campaign selling the same offer regardless of series or creative angle.

series_id.description: Groups campaigns that are installments of the same narrative sequence (e.g. a sequel episode). Null when this campaign is a standalone, not part of a series.

time_zone.description: IANA zone the human-facing times are reasoned in, e.g. America/New_York. Drop times still carry their own explicit offset.

landing_url.description: Base CTA URL. UTM parameters are appended per drop. Defaults to the $199 Web Basics onboarding URL when omitted.

cadence.description: Human-readable record of how the drop times were derived. Documentation only; scheduled_time on each drop is authoritative.

publish_arming.description: Records which switch arms real sends. Informational: the runner reads the environment, never this block.

owner_override.description: Explicit owner authorization for a controlled flood run. The runner still requires the environment arming switch and confirmation.

channel_map.description: Optional per-campaign additions to the shared channel-label -> Postiz-integration map. Use when a campaign names a surface the shared map does not know.

copy_preference.description: Optional per-campaign override of which copy key each Postiz integration prefers, most specific first.

content_id.description: Idempotency key. Emitted as utm_content in the tracked link, which is how a rerun adopts an existing draft instead of duplicating a live post. Normally equal to drop_id.

scheduled_time.description: ISO 8601 WITH an explicit UTC offset, e.g. 2026-09-03T23:50:00-04:00. Absolute by design: a bare HH:MM cannot express a drop that crosses midnight, which is exactly how a late-night cadence gets mis-ordered.

channels.description: Channel labels resolved through the shared map plus any channel_map override. A requested channel that is not connected in Postiz is reported, never silently dropped.

primary_media.description: Repository-relative path. Resolved at run time on the host that runs the queue; a missing file blocks the drop by name rather than substituting or skipping.

backup_media.description: Stands in for a missing primary_media only. Never rescues a missing carousel slide.

copy.description: Channel-shaped copy variants keyed by audience surface (tiktok_reels_shorts, x_post, facebook_instagram, linkedin_facebook, x_thread_opener, all_channels). The runner picks the most specific key each integration prefers and appends the tracked link and tags.

provider_ids.description: Written back by the runner. Presence of postiz_draft_id makes a rerun idempotent.

provider_reconciliation.description: A source-plan correction that has not been reconciled against the provider. draft_retime_required is a hard local safety block: the queue runner will not adopt, queue, or schedule that drop until the provider record is deliberately reconciled.
